nightly-ci-bot: ALERT: nightly-performance check failed (small-batch p95 +18% vs baseline)
model: redwood/pythia-1.4b-q4
route: /generate (small-batch)
build: ci-nightly/2026-03-16-07:00 (id=ci-3449876501)
metric: p95 latency 310ms -> 365ms (+18%)
artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/nightly/2026-03-16/ci-3449876501/

mia: oh — thanks for the ping. does the alert include sample traces or flamegraphs? :eyes:

leo: I pulled the artifacts link, there's a `tail_latency` histogram and a few perf traces under `profiles/`. looks like CPU sys jumps during kv-cache evictions around sequence ~340. attaching sample path: `profiles/worker-3/trace-07-12-02.pb`

anya: pinging @leo — can you run a flamegraph and upload? I can start a quick reproduce locally if you get the exact run args.

leo: running `scripts/bench/flame.sh gs://redwood-bench/nightly/2026-03-16/ci-3449876501/profiles/worker-3/trace-07-12-02.pb` now. will share flamegraph url in a min.

sam: flagging that we merged scheduler change from PR#987 yesterday (deferred-preempt). cc @ops-oncall in case it impacts kernel scheduling. maybe coincidence but worth checking.

ops-oncall: on it. spinning a duplicate bench in us-west2 with old scheduler flag (rollback) to A/B test. job id: ab-test-3449876610. keeping capacity until we have result.

mia: can someone post the exact bench invocation used by the nightly job? I want to run a local repro with the same seeds.

leo: nightly invocation from ci metadata: 
```
./ci/run_bench.sh --model=pythia-1.4b-q4 --batch=4 --seq=512 --workload=small-batch --sample-rate=0.02 --kv-cache=true --profiling=perf
```
run-id: ci-3449876501

anya: I'll try that locally with `--profile=cpu` and the same seed. if I can reproduce, I'll attach perf.data and a diff of symbols.

sam: quick thought — memory pressure could increase sys time from more page faults on eviction. any memory footprint diffs in the artifact?

leo: preliminary flamegraph looks like a big wedge in `page_fault_handler` + `evict_kv_cache` (custom layer). sharing: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/flames/ci-3449876501/worker-3.html :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: A/B job finished: ab-test-3449876610 (with scheduler rollback) p95=318ms, almost back to baseline. baseline 310ms, nightly 365ms, rollback 318ms. looks correlated to scheduler change.

mia: ok that nails it directionally. next steps: create a bisect of the scheduler change and run a targeted bench to confirm. @leo can you open the bisect CI with commits starting at commit a1b2..f9e8 and include `--workload small-batch`?

leo: will do. creating job `ci/bisect/scheduler-344987` and scheduling tests. assigning to myself. ETA ~45m.

anya: nice. I'll hold off on deeper syscall profiling until bisect narrows commits. if bisect points elsewhere I'll dig in.

sam: if bisect confirms, we should revert the scheduler flag and re-run nightly, then ship a follow-up PR with safer logic + regression tests.

mia: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident tracker with the current hypothesis (scheduler change) and link artifacts. leaving this thread as the source of truth for the triage. :white_check_mark:

leo: bisect started: https://ci.redwood.ai/bisect/scheduler-344987 (job queued). will update here when complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

nightly-ci-bot: NOTE: rerun scheduled by ops-oncall (ab-test-3449876610).

mia: closing note — follow-ups: 1) confirm bisect result, 2) if confirmed, revert flag + run nightly, 3) add unit/regression test in ci for scheduler toggle. I'll create the follow-up ticket.

sam: copy. thanks all. :thumbsup:

leo: update: bisect narrowed to PR#987 -> cause confirmed. opening revert PR now (will link).

ops-oncall: deployed rollback to staging, monitoring for further regressions.

mia: excellent. I'll mark triage as resolved once revert PR is merged and nightly stabilizes.

leo: revert PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/runtime/pull/1005 — requesting review from @sam.

sam: reviewing now.

mia: thread resolved for now. cheers.
